name: Coastal Data Information Program
provider: Scripps Institution of Oceanography (UC San Diego)
description: Long-running network of wave-measurement buoys providing near-real-time and historic directional wave, sea surface temperature, and wave-model data, served via THREDDS and ERDDAP.
spatial_coverage: U.S. coasts (Pacific, Atlantic, Gulf, Great Lakes, Pacific Islands)
variables: significant wave height, peak/mean wave period, wave direction, directional wave spectra, sea surface temperature, wave-model output
notes: Operated by Scripps with U.S. Army Corps of Engineers and California DPR support; buoys transmit via Iridium every 30 minutes.

name: CUAHSI HydroShare
provider: Consortium of Universities for the Advancement of Hydrologic Science, Inc. (CUAHSI)
description: Online repository for sharing hydrologic and water-related data and models, including coastal and critical-zone datasets, with a public RESTful web-service API (hsapi) and the hsclient Python package.
spatial_coverage: Global (primarily United States)
variables: hydrologic time series, geospatial rasters/features, model programs and instances, multidimensional NetCDF, coastal/critical-zone datasets
notes: REST API follows OpenAPI standards; hsclient wraps the API for resource discovery, download, and update. DOIs minted for formally published resources.

endpoints.label: HydroShare REST API (hsapi)
endpoints.format_notes: OpenAPI/JSON; resource CRUD and file access

name: Coastal Critical Zone / Critical Zone Collaborative Network
provider: NSF Critical Zone Collaborative Network (Coastal Thematic Cluster)
description: NSF-funded network studying coupled land-sea margin critical-zone processes; the Coastal cluster consolidates coastal data, published and discoverable through the CZCN Hub and CUAHSI HydroShare.
spatial_coverage: U.S. coastal land-sea transition zones
variables: groundwater, soil moisture/chemistry, hydrology, biogeochemical fluxes, salinity intrusion, sediment/elemental cycling
notes: Data are distributed across HydroShare, EarthChem, SESAR, OpenTopography, Zenodo and DataONE; licensing varies by resource. HydroShare exposes a public REST API (hsapi).

name: Coastal Carbon Network / Coastal Carbon Atlas
provider: Smithsonian Environmental Research Center (SERC)
description: The Coastal Carbon Network compiles an open-source synthesis of soil carbon data from tidal wetlands worldwide (marsh, mangrove, seagrass, tidal freshwater/swamp), with the Data Library holding thousands of standardized soil profiles across dozens of countries. The Coastal Carbon Atlas is an interactive Shiny map application to visualize, query, and download the library, and open-source R workflows and compiled files are published on GitHub.
spatial_coverage: Global tidal/coastal wetlands (all continents except Antarctica)
variables: soil organic carbon, carbon stock/density, dry bulk density, loss-on-ignition organic matter, core depth intervals, accretion/dating (137Cs, 210Pb), habitat and site metadata
update_frequency: periodic versioned releases (e.g., Data Library v1.5.0)
notes: Library spans decades of soil cores; DOI points to the versioned Coastal Carbon Library on Smithsonian Figshare. Source data and code are maintained on GitHub.

endpoints.label: Coastal Carbon Data Library and Atlas
Coastal Carbon Atlas (interactive app)
endpoints.format_notes: query/visualize/download subsets of the Data Library

endpoints.label: CCN Data Library GitHub API
endpoints.format_notes: programmatic access to synthesis repo (raw CSV workflows and compiled files)

name: Copernicus Marine Service
provider: Mercator Ocean International / European Commission (Copernicus)
description: European operational service providing global and regional ocean observations, reanalyses, and forecasts through the Copernicus Marine Data Store, with a STAC-backed Python/CLI toolbox and cloud subsetting.
spatial_coverage: Global oceans and European seas
license: Copernicus Marine Service license (free, attribution required)
variables: sea surface temperature, salinity, sea surface height, ocean currents, sea ice, chlorophyll/biogeochemistry, waves, ocean forecasts and reanalyses
notes: Coastal relevance via regional (EU seas) products; global coverage overall. Programmatic access is via the copernicusmarine toolbox which parses the STAC catalog; free registration required for downloads.

endpoints.label: Copernicus Marine STAC catalog
endpoints.format_notes: STAC catalog backing the copernicusmarine toolbox

name: NOAA Coastal Change Analysis Program Regional Land Cover
provider: NOAA Office for Coastal Management
description: Nationally standardized, raster-based land cover and land cover change products (30 m) for the coastal regions of the conterminous U.S., updated on a roughly 5-year cycle.
spatial_coverage: Coastal conterminous United States (plus territories)
variables: 25-class land cover, land cover change, impervious surface, wetlands, developed/agriculture/forest classes

name: NOAA C-CAP High-Resolution Land Cover
provider: NOAA Office for Coastal Management
description: 1-meter resolution land cover, impervious surface, and change products derived by C-CAP for the coastal U.S., a higher-resolution companion to the 30 m regional product.
spatial_coverage: Coastal United States (selected regions/states)
variables: 1-m land cover, impervious surface, tree canopy, land cover change
notes: Coverage and vintages vary by region; distributed alongside the regional product on Digital Coast.

name: Estimating the Circulation and Climate of the Ocean (ECCO)
provider: NASA JPL / ECCO Consortium via PO.DAAC
description: ECCO is a data-assimilating global ocean/sea-ice state estimate that fits a free-running ocean model to satellite and in-situ observations while satisfying physical conservation laws, yielding a dynamically consistent full-depth reconstruction. The V4r4 release provides global fields over 1992-2018 at daily and monthly intervals on both the native LLC90 grid and a 0.5-degree lat-lon grid.
spatial_coverage: Global ocean, full depth
license: NASA open data / U.S. public domain (Earthdata login required)
variables: ocean velocity, potential temperature, salinity, sea surface height, ocean bottom pressure, sea ice concentration/thickness, heat/volume/freshwater fluxes

endpoints.label: ECCO project page at PO.DAAC
endpoints.format_notes: links to ~79 V4r4 dataset landing pages

endpoints.label: JPL OPeNDAP
endpoints.format_notes: OPeNDAP access to ECCO netCDF fields

name: European Marine Observation and Data Network
provider: European Commission (DG MARE)
description: European gateway to marine data organized by thematic areas (bathymetry, biology, chemistry, geology, human activities, physics, seabed habitats), delivering interoperable products through OGC WMS/WFS/WPS and CSW services.
spatial_coverage: European seas
variables: bathymetry, seabed habitats, marine biology / species distribution, chemistry, geology, human activities, physical parameters
notes: Each thematic lot serves OGC-compliant WMS/WFS/CSW endpoints (e.g. ows.emodnet-humanactivities.eu, ows.emodnet-bathymetry.eu); a unified EMODnet geoviewer aggregates layers.

endpoints.label: EMODnet portal
endpoints.format_notes: thematic portals and unified map viewer

name: Global Biodiversity Information Facility
provider: GBIF Secretariat
description: International open-data infrastructure aggregating species occurrence and checklist records worldwide; the coastal/marine subset is queryable through the GBIF REST API by taxonomy, geometry, and environment.
spatial_coverage: Global
variables: species occurrence, taxonomy, coordinates, event date, basis of record, dataset metadata (Darwin Core)
notes: OBIS marine records are also shared to GBIF. Occurrence search paged at max 300/page with a 100,000-record offset limit; bulk pulls via the Download API.

name: GBIF Occurrence API (marine records)
provider: Global Biodiversity Information Facility Secretariat
description: The Global Biodiversity Information Facility provides free, open access to biodiversity occurrence data aggregated from thousands of institutions worldwide, including extensive marine species records (many shared jointly with OBIS). The REST API (api.gbif.org/v1) supports programmatic search, faceting, and asynchronous download of occurrence records, filterable to marine taxa and datasets.
spatial_coverage: Global (terrestrial and marine); marine subset via taxon/dataset/environment filters
variables: species occurrence records (scientific name, taxonKey, lat/lon, event date, basis of record, depth), dataset provenance

endpoints.label: GBIF REST API v1
endpoints.format_notes: JSON; /occurrence/search?..., /occurrence/download (POST, auth for downloads); marine filter via taxonKey/datasetKey

name: Coastal Observing Data & Information Sharing for Security (CODISS)
provider: U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Science & Technology Directorate
description: Homeland-security coastal surveillance and maritime-domain information-sharing capability. Related DHS S&T work (Coastal Surveillance System / IMDE) fuses sensor feeds for law-enforcement use rather than open public data distribution.
spatial_coverage: U.S. coastal waters (maritime domain awareness)
notes: The exact 'CODISS' acronym could not be verified against a public data endpoint via web search. DHS S&T operates a Coastal Surveillance System (CSS) / Integrated Maritime Domain Enterprise for maritime domain awareness, which is a restricted law-enforcement information-sharing platform, not an open data program. Record retained per instructions with a portal-only endpoint.

endpoints.label: DHS S&T Port & Coastal Surveillance fact sheet
endpoints.format_notes: informational only; no public data API

name: Global Ocean Observing System
provider: Intergovernmental Oceanographic Commission of UNESCO
description: The international framework coordinating sustained ocean observations of physics, biogeochemistry, and biology/ecosystems across platforms, defined around Essential Ocean Variables. It is the global umbrella under which U.S. IOOS and other national systems contribute; operational status and metadata are tracked through OceanOPS.
spatial_coverage: Global
variables: Essential Ocean Variables — temperature, salinity, currents, sea level, oxygen, nutrients, inorganic carbon, phytoplankton, zooplankton

name: Alaska Ocean Observing System
provider: Alaska Ocean Observing System (AOOS); hosted by the University of Alaska Fairbanks
description: AOOS is the IOOS Regional Association for Alaska, integrating real-time and historical ocean and coastal observations across the Gulf of Alaska, Bering Sea, Aleutians, and Arctic. Its Ocean Data Explorer portal and Axiom-operated ERDDAP server provide access to buoys, moorings, gliders, tide/water-level stations, HF radar, and model output.
spatial_coverage: Alaska: Arctic Ocean, Bering Sea, Gulf of Alaska, and Alaskan coastal waters
variables: sea temperature, salinity, water level, waves, currents, wind, air temperature, dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll, ocean acidification (pH, pCO2)
notes: temporal_start is the approximate founding year of the RA, not a dataset start date.

name: Caribbean Coastal Ocean Observing System
provider: Caribbean Coastal Ocean Observing System (CariCOOS); University of Puerto Rico at Mayaguez
description: CARICOOS is the IOOS Regional Association serving Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands, operating data buoys, coastal met stations, HF radar, gliders, and numerical models. Data flow through a THREDDS server (WMS/WCS/OPeNDAP) and an ERDDAP data server, with a public data-download portal as the main human entry point.
spatial_coverage: U.S. Caribbean: Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands
variables: waves, currents (HF radar), temperature, salinity, wind, sea surface temperature, glider profiles
notes: ERDDAP is served from dm3.caricoos.org; THREDDS is mirrored across dm1/dm2 hosts. temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

endpoints.label: CARICOOS Data Download
endpoints.format_notes: human entry point linking THREDDS + ERDDAP

name: Central and Northern California Ocean Observing System
provider: Central and Northern California Ocean Observing System (CeNCOOS); Monterey Bay Aquarium Research Institute (MBARI)
description: CeNCOOS is the IOOS Regional Association for central and northern California, delivering coastal observations, model forecasts, and integrated products. Its data management is run with Axiom Data Science: time-series data are served via the CeNCOOS ERDDAP server and gridded/model data via THREDDS, with the shared California (CalOOS) Data Portal as the main human interface.
spatial_coverage: Central and northern California coast (Oregon border to Point Conception)
variables: temperature, salinity, currents (HF radar), HABs, ocean acidification, dissolved oxygen, nutrients, water quality, glider profiles
notes: Shares the statewide California Ocean Observing Systems Data Portal (data.caloos.org) with SCCOOS. temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

endpoints.label: California Ocean Observing Systems Data Portal

name: Gulf of Mexico Coastal Ocean Observing System
provider: Gulf of Mexico Coastal Ocean Observing System (GCOOS); Texas A&M University
description: GCOOS is the IOOS Regional Association for the Gulf of Mexico, aggregating observations from federal and non-federal buoys, moorings, gliders, HF radar, and model output. It operates multiple ERDDAP servers behind a central data portal that lets users discover and download station and gridded datasets across the Gulf.
spatial_coverage: Gulf of Mexico (U.S. Gulf coast and offshore waters)
variables: sea temperature, salinity, currents, waves, water level, wind, air temperature, dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll, nutrients, harmful algal bloom indicators
notes: Main data portal at data.gcoos.org links to multiple ERDDAP and THREDDS instances. temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

name: Great Lakes Observing System
provider: Great Lakes Observing System (GLOS); Ann Arbor, Michigan
description: GLOS is the IOOS Regional Association for the Great Lakes, providing IOOS-certified data and metadata from buoys, weather stations, and model nowcasts/forecasts. Its cloud-based Seagull platform (launched 2022) delivers data through a web console and a public REST API (e.g. /api/v1/obs-dataset-summaries, /api/v1/parameters).
spatial_coverage: Laurentian Great Lakes (Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario) and connecting waters
variables: water temperature, waves, currents, water level, dissolved oxygen, weather, ice, buoy observations
notes: Public data portal is the Seagull platform (seagull.glos.org). temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

endpoints.label: Seagull REST API
endpoints.format_notes: endpoints incl. /obs-dataset-summaries, /parameters; base path corroborated from GLOS docs but exact base URL not directly fetched (medium)

name: Mid-Atlantic Regional Association Coastal Ocean Observing System
provider: Mid-Atlantic Regional Association Coastal Ocean Observing System (MARACOOS); Rutgers University
description: MARACOOS is the IOOS Regional Association for the Mid-Atlantic Bight, integrating satellite SST/ocean color, HF radar surface currents, gliders, buoys, and model forecasts. Data are served via a MARACOOS ERDDAP server and an OceansMap EDS THREDDS/OPeNDAP server, with the OceansMap web application as the primary visualization portal.
spatial_coverage: U.S. Mid-Atlantic Bight (Cape Cod, MA to Cape Hatteras, NC)
variables: currents (HF radar), sea surface temperature (satellite), ocean color, temperature, salinity, waves, water level, glider profiles
notes: Public portal is OceansMap (oceansmap.maracoos.org). THREDDS exists but its exact URL was not independently verified. temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

name: Northwest Association of Networked Ocean Observing Systems
provider: Northwest Association of Networked Ocean Observing Systems (NANOOS); University of Washington
description: NANOOS is the Pacific Northwest (Washington, Oregon, and adjacent coastal and estuarine waters) Regional Association of the U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System. It aggregates near-real-time buoy, mooring, shore-station, glider, HF radar, and model data through the NANOOS Visualization System (NVS) Data Explorer and serves them via ERDDAP and OGC web services.
spatial_coverage: U.S. Pacific Northwest coast and estuaries (Washington, Oregon), including Salish Sea and adjacent Northeast Pacific
license: Public domain / open (varies by provider); NOAA-funded
variables: temperature, salinity, currents (HF radar), waves, ocean acidification, dissolved oxygen, water level, mooring and glider profiles
notes: ERDDAP reachable at both data.nanoos.org/erddap and erddap.nanoos.org. Public portal is the NANOOS Visualization System (NVS). temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

name: Northeastern Regional Association of Coastal Ocean Observing Systems
provider: Northeastern Regional Association of Coastal Ocean Observing Systems (NERACOOS)
description: NERACOOS is the Northeast U.S. and Canadian Maritimes Regional Association of the U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System, operating the Gulf of Maine Ocean Observing Array and aggregating regional buoy, mooring, shore-station, HF radar, and model data. Time-series and gridded data are served through ERDDAP and a THREDDS Data Server.
spatial_coverage: Northeast U.S. and Canadian Maritime coastal/ocean waters, including the Gulf of Maine, Georges Bank, Long Island Sound, and Scotian Shelf
license: Public domain / open (varies by provider); NOAA-funded
variables: water temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, currents, waves, sea surface temperature, chlorophyll, meteorology (wind, air temperature, pressure)
notes: Successor to the Gulf of Maine Ocean Observing System (GoMOOS). temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

endpoints.label: NERACOOS THREDDS Data Server
endpoints.format_notes: OPeNDAP/NCSS/WMS access to buoy and model netCDF datasets

name: Pacific Islands Ocean Observing System
provider: Pacific Islands Ocean Observing System (PacIOOS); University of Hawaii at Manoa
description: PacIOOS is the Pacific Islands Regional Association of the U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System, hosted at the University of Hawaii School of Ocean and Earth Science and Technology (SOEST). It serves in-situ observations, ROMS/WaveWatch III forecast model output, satellite remote sensing, and bathymetry through ERDDAP and a THREDDS Data Server.
spatial_coverage: U.S. Pacific Islands region: Hawaii, Guam, CNMI, American Samoa, freely associated states (Marshall Islands, FSM, Palau), and U.S. minor outlying islands
license: Public domain / open (varies by provider); NOAA-funded
variables: water temperature, salinity, currents, waves, sea level, sea surface temperature, chlorophyll, wave/ocean model forecasts, bathymetry/DEM, water quality
update_frequency: near real-time in-situ; daily model/satellite updates
notes: ERDDAP serves in-situ data; THREDDS serves gridded model, satellite, and bathymetry data. temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

name: Southern California Coastal Ocean Observing System
provider: Southern California Coastal Ocean Observing System (SCCOOS); Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego
description: SCCOOS is the Southern California Regional Association of the U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System, coordinated through Scripps Institution of Oceanography. It operates automated shore stations, HF radar surface-current mapping, and the CalHABMAP harmful-algal-bloom monitoring network, serving data through its own ERDDAP and the shared California (CeNCOOS+SCCOOS) CalOOS data portal.
spatial_coverage: Southern and central California coastal ocean (U.S. West Coast), with statewide integration via the California Ocean Observing Systems (CalOOS) portal
license: Public domain / open (varies by provider); NOAA-funded
variables: temperature, salinity, currents (HF radar), HABs, water quality, ocean acidification, automated shore-station data, glider profiles
notes: Shares the statewide California Ocean Observing Systems Data Portal (data.caloos.org) with CeNCOOS; also runs the SCCOOS Data Portal at portal.sccoos.org. temporal_start is approximate RA founding year.

endpoints.label: CalOOS (California Ocean Observing Systems) Data Portal
endpoints.format_notes: Axiom-hosted shared California data portal (SCCOOS + CeNCOOS)

name: Southeast Coastal Ocean Observing Regional Association
provider: Southeast Coastal Ocean Observing Regional Association (SECOORA); Charleston, South Carolina
description: SECOORA is the Southeast U.S. Regional Association of the U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System, a non-profit based in Charleston, SC, covering the coastal waters of North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, and Florida. It aggregates buoy, shore-station, HF radar, and model data through an Axiom-developed data portal and serves time-series data via ERDDAP.
spatial_coverage: Southeast U.S. coastal and offshore waters: North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, and Florida (including Gulf of Mexico Florida coast)
license: Public domain / open (varies by provider); NOAA-funded
variables: water temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, currents, waves, sea surface temperature, HF radar surface currents, meteorology, water quality, coastal circulation model output
notes: temporal_start is approximate RA founding/incorporation year.

endpoints.label: SECOORA ERDDAP (Axiom-hosted)
endpoints.format_notes: tabledap for time-series; CSV, JSON, netCDF, graphs

name: IOOS Environmental Sensor Map ERDDAP
provider: U.S. IOOS Program Office (NOAA)
description: ERDDAP server aggregating regional, national, and global real-time in-situ sensor data across the IOOS enterprise, feeding the Environmental Sensor Map data portal.
spatial_coverage: United States and global real-time in-situ sensors
variables: water temperature, salinity, waves, winds, currents, water level, meteorology, water quality

name: Permanent Service for Mean Sea Level
provider: National Oceanography Centre (UK)
description: The global data bank for long-term sea-level change from coastal tide gauges, providing Revised Local Reference (RLR) and metric monthly and annual mean sea-level records used for sea-level trend analysis worldwide. Directly supports the target's Sea Level Change focus and complements NOAA CO-OPS and UHSLC.
spatial_coverage: Global coastal tide gauges
variables: monthly and annual mean sea level (tide-gauge RLR and metric)

endpoints.label: PSMSL data obtaining page (RLR/metric monthly and annual files)

name: Ocean Biodiversity Information System
provider: IOC-UNESCO (International Oceanographic Data and Information Exchange, IODE)
program: International Oceanographic Data and Information Exchange (IODE)
description: A global open-access data system and clearing-house for marine biodiversity, coordinated by IOC-UNESCO, that aggregates and standardizes species occurrence records (Darwin Core) from thousands of datasets worldwide. Data are queryable through a documented REST API and an online mapper.
spatial_coverage: Global oceans
variables: species occurrence, taxonomy, abundance, presence/absence, event date, location (Darwin Core), measurement-or-fact
update_frequency: Continuous (rolling contributions and periodic full rebuilds)
notes: Founded 2000 under the Census of Marine Life; now an IODE programme. Full snapshot also on AWS Open Data as GeoParquet.

name: Coastal LTER Site Data via EDI Data Portal
provider: Environmental Data Initiative (EDI) / U.S. LTER Network
description: Umbrella access to long-term ecological research data from coastal LTER sites (Virginia Coast Reserve, Georgia Coastal Ecosystems, Plum Island Ecosystems, Florida Coastal Everglades, Santa Barbara Coastal) archived and served through the EDI Data Portal and PASTA+ repository.
spatial_coverage: U.S. coastal LTER sites (VCR, GCE, PIE, FCE, SBC)
variables: vegetation/marsh dynamics, water quality, nutrients, primary productivity, hydrography, meteorology, elevation/geomorphology (site-specific)
notes: Data organized as EML-described data packages; each package carries its own DOI. Licensing is mostly CC-BY-4.0 but varies by package.

name: Smithsonian MarineGEO (Marine Global Earth Observatory)
provider: Smithsonian Institution, Tennenbaum Marine Observatories Network
description: A global network of coastal observatories that tracks marine biodiversity and ecosystem change using standardized, coordinated protocols. Biological survey data are curated centrally and published to open repositories such as OBIS.
spatial_coverage: Global coastal (network of partner observatories worldwide)
variables: biodiversity, seagrass/habitat monitoring, epifauna, predation assays, fish/invertebrate community composition, water quality
notes: MarineGEO has no single open machine API; standardized data flow to OBIS/GBIF and protocols/templates are published on Figshare and marinegeo.github.io. Licensing varies by dataset.

endpoints.label: OBIS API (MarineGEO datasets published to OBIS)

name: NASA Sea Level Change Portal
provider: NASA Sea Level Change Team / JPL
description: NASA's portal aggregating sea level observations, ice observations, and model output with interactive analysis and projection tools, plus programmatic statistics services (NEXUS/SDAP).
spatial_coverage: Global
variables: global mean sea level, sea level anomaly, ice mass, sea level projections (IPCC AR6), regional sea level

name: NASA Ocean Biology Distributed Active Archive Center (OceanColor Web)
provider: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center, Ocean Biology Processing Group
description: NASA's archive and distribution node for ocean-color satellite products (CZCS, SeaWiFS, MODIS-Aqua/Terra, VIIRS, PACE/OCI). Delivers chlorophyll-a, remote-sensing reflectance, diffuse attenuation, and SST products central to coastal water-quality and primary-production monitoring — the 'NASA Coastal Processes' data stream implied by the target coverage.
spatial_coverage: Global oceans and coastal waters
license: NASA open data — free and open, effectively public domain
variables: chlorophyll-a, remote-sensing reflectance (Rrs), diffuse attenuation Kd490, particulate organic carbon, sea surface temperature, aerosol optical thickness

endpoints.label: OceanData OPeNDAP server
endpoints.format_notes: NetCDF/HDF products; Earthdata Login required for some collections

name: NASA Common Metadata Repository
provider: NASA EOSDIS / ESDIS
description: NASA's high-performance metadata catalog for Earth-observing data (including all EOSDIS DAACs plus partner agencies), providing REST search APIs for collections, granules, and services with keyword, spatial, temporal, and faceted queries.
spatial_coverage: Global
variables: collection metadata, granule metadata, service metadata, spatial/temporal extents, data access URLs
notes: Underlies Earthdata Search and PO.DAAC discovery; also exposes an OpenSearch interface and GraphQL. Search is anonymous; data downloads generally require Earthdata Login.

name: NASA Physical Oceanography Distributed Active Archive Center
provider: NASA / Jet Propulsion Laboratory (EOSDIS)
description: PO.DAAC is NASA's data center for physical oceanography satellite and model data, archiving and distributing sea surface temperature, ocean topography/sea surface height, salinity, ocean winds, sea ice, and circulation products. Machine access is provided via the Earthdata Common Metadata Repository (CMR) for discovery, Harmony for on-the-fly transformation/subsetting, OPeNDAP, and THREDDS.
spatial_coverage: Global oceans
license: NASA open data / U.S. public domain (Earthdata login required for many downloads)
variables: sea surface temperature, sea surface height/altimetry, sea surface salinity, ocean surface winds, ocean currents, gravimetry, SWOT water elevation
notes: On-premises services retired; all data distributed via Earthdata Cloud. Requires a free NASA Earthdata Login; direct S3 access requires us-west-2 AWS credentials.

endpoints.label: OPeNDAP in the Cloud
endpoints.format_notes: single interface to Earthdata cloud OPeNDAP

endpoints.label: Earthdata CMR search API
endpoints.format_notes: programmatic collection/granule discovery incl. OPeNDAP URLs

endpoints.label: Earthdata Cloud OPeNDAP (POCLOUD)
endpoints.format_notes: Hyrax OPeNDAP for cloud-hosted PO.DAAC collections

name: NASA PO.DAAC Coastal Altimetry / Sea Surface Height Products
provider: NASA JPL Physical Oceanography Distributed Active Archive Center
description: NASA's physical oceanography data center distributing satellite sea surface height and coastal altimetry products (retracked/corrected for coastal and inland waters), including gridded MEaSUREs SSHA and SWOT.
spatial_coverage: Global ocean and coastal zones
variables: sea surface height, sea level anomaly, coastal altimetry, gridded SSHA, ocean surface topography
notes: Data are distributed via NASA Earthdata Cloud; discovery/subsetting via CMR and download typically require a free Earthdata Login. Individual products carry their own DOIs.

endpoints.label: NASA CMR search API
endpoints.format_notes: REST; find/subset granules (netCDF); Earthdata Login for download

name: NASA Sea Level Change Portal
provider: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)
description: NASA's public gateway to sea level change science, aggregating satellite altimetry, GRACE/GRACE-FO mass change, and in-situ records into interactive data-analysis tools and downloadable time series. It also hosts IPCC AR6 sea level projection tools and a statistics/analysis service that returns gridded and point sea level data as JSON or CSV.
spatial_coverage: Global ocean, with regional/local projection tools
license: NASA open data / U.S. public domain (Earthdata login may be required for some products)
variables: mean sea level, sea surface height anomaly, ocean mass, land water storage, steric sea level, sea level projections
update_frequency: periodic (satellite record and analysis tools updated as new cycles are processed)

endpoints.label: Sea Level Change Portal home
endpoints.format_notes: human entry point; links to data tools and downloads

endpoints.label: Sea Level Change Portal statistics services (NEXUS)
endpoints.format_notes: returns time-series/statistics output in JSON or CSV

name: NCEI Natural Hazards — Tsunami, Earthquake & Volcano Databases (former NGDC)
provider: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI, formerly National Geophysical Data Center)
description: NOAA's authoritative historical hazards databases covering tsunami events and runups, significant earthquakes, and significant volcanic eruptions, plus related coastal DART deep-ocean assessment data. Records span from deep antiquity to present and are searchable through the HazEL viewer and a hazard-service REST API.
spatial_coverage: Global, with detailed US coastal tsunami runup records
license: U.S. Government work / public domain (NOAA open data)
variables: tsunami events, tsunami runup heights, significant earthquakes, significant volcanic eruptions, DART deep-ocean tsunami detection

endpoints.label: HazEL tsunami event search
endpoints.format_notes: human search UI over global historical tsunami database

endpoints.label: NCEI HazEL hazard-service REST API
endpoints.format_notes: JSON queries for tsunamis/earthquakes/volcanoes; exact version path unverified

endpoints.label: NCEI Natural Hazards product landing page

name: NCEI World Ocean Database
provider: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information
description: The world's largest collection of uniformly formatted, quality-controlled ocean profile data (temperature, salinity, oxygen, nutrients, chlorophyll) from bottles, CTDs, XBTs, gliders, profiling floats, and moorings. Foundation for the World Ocean Atlas climatologies and a core reference archive for coastal-to-open-ocean hydrography.
spatial_coverage: Global
variables: temperature, salinity, dissolved oxygen, phosphate, nitrate, silicate, chlorophyll, pH, alkalinity

endpoints.label: NCEI ocean THREDDS catalog
endpoints.format_notes: NetCDF WOD/WOA products; exact sub-catalog path may vary

name: NOAA Operational Model Archive and Distribution System
provider: NOAA / National Centers for Environmental Prediction (NCEP)
description: NOAA framework for remote access to high-volume numerical weather-prediction and ocean/climate model output (including coastal and ocean forecast domains) via THREDDS/OPeNDAP, a GrADS Data Server, and GRIB filter services.
spatial_coverage: Global (with regional and coastal model domains)
variables: atmospheric and ocean model fields (winds, waves, SST, currents, precipitation, pressure, geopotential), NWP and ocean forecast gridded output
update_frequency: multiple cycles per day (per model run)
notes: Real-time server at nomads.ncep.noaa.gov (24x7 by NCEP); near-real-time archive historically via NCEI. THREDDS/OPeNDAP served through the GrADS Data Server (/dods).

update_frequency: Ongoing coordinated campaigns; data submitted and released on a rolling basis

endpoints.format_notes: Primary human entry point; central data submission is currently email-based (marinegeo-data@si.edu), no public ERDDAP/tabledap endpoint was corroborated via search

endpoints.label: MarineGEO data tools, standards, and protocols site
endpoints.format_notes: Data standards, submission templates, and R tooling (e.g. marinegeo-data-tracker); protocols also archived on Smithsonian Figshare

name: Coastal Data Information Program
provider: Scripps Institution of Oceanography, UC San Diego
program: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers / California Dept. of Parks & Recreation (funders)
description: A network of nearshore Datawell Waverider buoys measuring directional wave spectra and sea surface temperature in near real-time, plus an operational wave model. Provides an extensive observed and modeled archive dating to the 1970s via THREDDS (NetCDF) and ERDDAP.
spatial_coverage: U.S. coasts (Pacific, Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico, Great Lakes, Pacific Islands) and select international sites
variables: significant wave height, peak/mean wave period, peak/mean wave direction, directional wave spectra, sea surface temperature

endpoints.label: CDIP THREDDS (realtime/archive/model NetCDF)
endpoints.format_notes: OPeNDAP, OGC SOS; archive at .../cdip/archive/catalog.html with per-deployment and historic.nc aggregates

name: IOOS National Glider Data Assembly Center
provider: U.S. IOOS / NOAA (hosted at Rutgers, archived at NCEI)
description: Centralized assembly center where glider operators submit autonomous underwater glider profiles for standardization, distribution over the WMO Global Telecommunications System, and archival at NCEI. Holds roughly 2,100 glider deployment datasets served through ERDDAP and THREDDS.
spatial_coverage: Global (U.S. and international underwater glider deployments)
license: U.S. Government data / public domain (no access restrictions)
variables: temperature, salinity, conductivity, density, pressure, depth; some gliders add dissolved oxygen, chlorophyll/fluorescence, CDOM, backscatter

endpoints.label: Glider DAC ERDDAP
endpoints.format_notes: tabledap; CSV, JSON, NetCDF; RESTful web services

name: Marine Biodiversity Observation Network
provider: U.S. Integrated Ocean Observing System (IOOS)
description: A network that coordinates the collection, integration, and sharing of marine biodiversity observations (from microbes to megafauna) to detect and understand change across U.S. and global waters, developed under U.S. IOOS and connected to the global GEO BON and GOOS frameworks. Standardized biodiversity products are served through IOOS-affiliated ERDDAP servers, OBIS/GBIF, and the MBON data portals.
spatial_coverage: U.S. regional MBON sites (e.g., Florida Keys, Santa Barbara Channel, Monterey Bay, Chukchi/Arctic) and global partner network
license: Varies by contributing project (often CC-BY / Public Domain)
variables: biodiversity, species occurrence, productivity, genomics/eDNA, phenology, habitat characterization, satellite-derived variables
notes: Biological data flow to OBIS/GBIF; the MBON Data Portal (built on the AXIOM Research Workspace) integrates real-time conditions, satellite, and biodiversity layers.

endpoints.label: MBON biological records via OBIS API

name: IOOS High Frequency Radar National Network (HFRNet)
provider: U.S. IOOS with Scripps Coastal Observing R&D Center (CORDC) and NOAA NDBC
description: National network of shore-based high-frequency radars measuring near-real-time ocean surface currents around U.S. coasts. A central node aggregates station radials into hourly gridded surface-current maps used for search-and-rescue, spill response, and coastal circulation studies. A major coastal observing asset absent from the current catalog.
spatial_coverage: U.S. coastal waters (all coasts plus Puerto Rico and Hawaii)
variables: sea-surface current velocity (u/v), radial velocities

name: Coastal LTER Datasets in the Environmental Data Initiative Repository
provider: Environmental Data Initiative (EDI)
description: EDI is the trusted repository (built on the PASTA+ software stack, co-developed with the US LTER Network) that curates and disseminates long-term ecological data, including coastal and estuarine LTER sites such as VCR, GCE, PIE, FCE, SBC, CCE, PAL, MCR, and NGA. Data packages are EML-described and served through the PASTA+ Data Package Manager REST API, with the EDI Data Portal as the human interface.
spatial_coverage: United States LTER coastal/estuarine and open-ocean sites (global partner sites also present)
license: typically CC0 or CC-BY per data package (declared in EML)
variables: site-dependent: water quality, nutrients, salinity/temperature, primary production, tides/hydrography, community ecology, biogeochemistry

endpoints.label: PASTA+ Data Package Manager REST API
endpoints.format_notes: EML metadata, data entities, and search; e.g. /metadata/eml/{scope}/{id}/{rev}

name: NSF National Ecological Observatory Network Data Portal
provider: Battelle (operated for the U.S. National Science Foundation)
description: A continental-scale ecological observatory whose aquatic sites (lakes, wadeable streams, and rivers, some near-coastal) provide standardized sensor and observational data products. The NEON Data API exposes products, sites, and sampling locations for programmatic access.
spatial_coverage: United States (20 ecoclimatic domains; ~34 aquatic sites among 81 total field sites)
license: Open (NEON data usage policy; free and open, attribution requested)
variables: water temperature, dissolved oxygen, specific conductance, pH, turbidity, chlorophyll, nitrate, stream discharge, surface-water chemistry, aquatic biology/taxonomy
update_frequency: sensor products roughly monthly release; ongoing

name: Ocean Observatories Initiative
provider: NSF; operated by Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution (with OSU, UW, Rutgers)
description: A long-term NSF-funded cabled and moored ocean observatory spanning coastal and global arrays, delivering multidisciplinary sensor time series. Data are freely available via the OOINet machine-to-machine (M2M) REST API, the Data Explorer / ERDDAP, and THREDDS.
spatial_coverage: Coastal and global arrays: NE Pacific (Endurance/Cabled), NW Atlantic (Pioneer), Irminger Sea; formerly Argentine Basin and Southern Ocean
license: Free and open (OOI data policy; effectively public domain / CC0)
variables: temperature, salinity, pressure, dissolved oxygen, pH, pCO2, nitrate, chlorophyll/fluorescence, currents/velocity, seismic, bottom pressure, meteorology

endpoints.label: OOINet M2M REST API
endpoints.format_notes: authenticated (API key/token); synchronous JSON or async NetCDF/CSV requests

endpoints.label: OOI Data Explorer THREDDS
endpoints.format_notes: OPeNDAP, NetCDF Subset; gold-copy NetCDF also at opendap.oceanobservatories.org/thredds/

name: USACE Field Research Facility (Duck, NC) Coastal Observations
provider: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), Coastal and Hydraulics Laboratory
program: USACE ERDC Coastal and Hydraulics Laboratory
description: Long-term nearshore coastal observatory at the Field Research Facility in Duck, North Carolina, operated by the USACE Coastal and Hydraulics Laboratory. Provides continuous measurements of waves, currents, water levels, winds, meteorology, and repeated nearshore bathymetry, served via the CHL THREDDS Data Server with OPeNDAP access.
spatial_coverage: Duck, NC nearshore, Atlantic Ocean
variables: waves (spectra, height, period, direction), currents, water levels, winds, meteorology, nearshore bathymetry

endpoints.label: CHL THREDDS Data Server (FRF catalog)
endpoints.format_notes: NetCDF FRF observation datasets; navigate to frf/ catalogs

endpoints.label: CHL THREDDS OPeNDAP endpoint
endpoints.format_notes: OPeNDAP (dodsC) access to FRF NetCDF datasets

endpoints.label: FRF website (human entry point)
endpoints.format_notes: Facility info, data catalog, and observation dashboards

name: USGS Coastal Change Hazards Portal
provider: U.S. Geological Survey
description: Interactive USGS web portal delivering nationally consistent coastal change hazard data, including long- and short-term shoreline (erosion) change rates, probabilities of storm-induced coastal change (dune collision, overwash, inundation), and coastal vulnerability to sea-level rise. Underlying datasets are published as USGS ScienceBase items with associated map/web services.
spatial_coverage: U.S. Atlantic, Gulf of Mexico, and Pacific open-ocean coasts (sandy shorelines)
variables: shoreline change rates, storm-induced coastal change probabilities (collision/overwash/inundation), coastal vulnerability index, extreme storm water levels
update_frequency: Periodic updates as regional analyses are revised

endpoints.label: Coastal Change Hazards Portal (human entry point)
ScienceBase items backing the portal layers
endpoints.format_notes: Portal layers are published ScienceBase items; query via /catalog/items?format=json

name: Coastal Storm Modeling System
provider: U.S. Geological Survey (Pacific Coastal and Marine Science Center)
description: A dynamic downscaling modeling system developed by USGS that predicts storm-induced coastal flooding, wave impacts, erosion, and cliff failure across large regions under a range of sea-level-rise and storm scenarios (e.g., CoSMoS for Southern/Central California, San Francisco Bay). Gridded model outputs are archived on USGS ScienceBase and made explorable through the Our Coast Our Future (OCOF) web tool.
spatial_coverage: U.S. West Coast focus (California coast and San Francisco Bay; expanding regions)
variables: flood extent and depth, wave height, water level, currents, cliff/beach erosion, wind, projected across sea-level-rise and storm scenarios
update_frequency: Episodic (new model releases per region/scenario set)

endpoints.label: Our Coast Our Future (OCOF) visualization/download tool
endpoints.format_notes: Interactive access to CoSMoS flood/erosion outputs

endpoints.label: CoSMoS model output archive on ScienceBase
endpoints.format_notes: Model outputs published as ScienceBase items; /catalog/items?format=json&q=CoSMoS

name: USGS Coastal and Marine Hazards and Resources Program
provider: U.S. Geological Survey
program: USGS Natural Hazards / Ecosystems Mission Areas
description: The USGS program that conducts research and long-term data collection on coastal and marine geology, geologic hazards (storms, tsunamis, sea-level rise, earthquakes), seafloor mapping, and marine mineral/energy resources for U.S. coasts and territorial waters. Datasets are cataloged and distributed through the USGS ScienceBase repository and the Coastal and Marine Geoscience Data System (CMGDS).
spatial_coverage: United States coastal zones, continental shelf, and marine EEZ (Atlantic, Pacific, Gulf of Mexico, Great Lakes, Alaska, Pacific/Caribbean territories)
variables: shoreline change, coastal erosion, storm-induced coastal change probabilities, sea-level rise, cliff retreat, seafloor mapping, coastal groundwater hazards
update_frequency: as assessments and surveys are released
notes: Portal organizes products under three themes (extreme storms, shoreline change, sea-level rise); underlying datasets are released and versioned in USGS ScienceBase.

endpoints.label: USGS Coastal Change Hazards Portal
endpoints.format_notes: interactive map viewer with data download

endpoints.label: CMHRP data releases via ScienceBase API
endpoints.format_notes: sbJSON item metadata and file downloads

endpoints.label: USGS ScienceBase catalog REST API
endpoints.format_notes: Item metadata/files via /catalog/item/{id}?format=json and search via /catalog/items?format=json&q=...

endpoints.label: Coastal and Marine Geoscience Data System (CMGDS) catalog
endpoints.format_notes: Successor to the marine.usgs.gov data catalog

name: OBIS-USA (U.S. Node of the Ocean Biodiversity Information System)
provider: U.S. Geological Survey, Science Analytics and Synthesis (SAS)
description: The United States national node of OBIS, managed by USGS, which assembles, standardizes (Darwin Core), and publishes U.S. marine biological occurrence data from federal, state, academic, and other sources for contribution to the global OBIS network. Data holdings are curated and served primarily through USGS ScienceBase.
spatial_coverage: United States and adjacent waters (Atlantic, Pacific, Gulf of Mexico, Alaska, territories)
license: Public Domain / CC-BY (varies by contributing dataset)
variables: species occurrence, abundance, presence/absence, taxonomy, sampling event (Darwin Core)
update_frequency: Periodic as datasets are contributed and republished
notes: Data best accessed through obis.org; source datasets and provenance staged in the USGS ScienceBase OBIS-USA community and an Integrated Publishing Toolkit (IPT); archived at NOAA NCEI.

endpoints.label: OBIS-USA data access
endpoints.format_notes: links to OBIS, IPT, and ScienceBase

endpoints.label: OBIS-USA data on USGS ScienceBase
endpoints.format_notes: OBIS-USA datasets published as ScienceBase items/collection; /catalog/items?format=json&q=OBIS-USA

endpoints.label: Global OBIS access to U.S. node records
endpoints.format_notes: OBIS-USA records are discoverable/served through the global OBIS portal and API

name: USGS ScienceBase
provider: U.S. Geological Survey
description: USGS's cross-program digital data repository and metadata catalog, hosting data releases, web services, and files from USGS programs including Coastal and Marine Hazards and Resources Program (CMHRP) coastal datasets. Named alongside CMHRP in the target coverage but is a distinct, general-purpose catalog with its own REST API.
spatial_coverage: Global (primarily United States)
license: Mostly public domain (U.S. Government works); item-level rights vary
variables: dataset metadata, geospatial files, coastal/marine data releases, tabular and raster attachments
notes: Append ?format=json to any item URL for sbJSON; REST endpoints support GET/POST/PUT/DELETE and item search. Python client: DOI-USGS/sciencebasepy.

endpoints.label: ScienceBase geospatial (WMS/WFS) services
endpoints.format_notes: per-item OGC services for spatial data
